```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmnet)
theme_set(theme_minimal())
set.seed(522)
```

# Summary



# Introduction

How accurately can we predict an order's estimated restaurant net margin in
US dollars using information available when the order is placed?



# Methods

## Data

We use the [Global Food Delivery & Restaurant Market 2026 dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/luthfimuthathohirin/global-food-delivery-restaurant-market-2026).
Our target is estimated restaurant net margin per order, measured in US dollars.



```{r}
# Create data folders.
dir.create("../data/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("../data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Download and extract the data.

url <- "https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/luthfimuthathohirin/global-food-delivery-restaurant-market-2026"
raw_file <- "../data/raw/global_food_delivery_enriched_market_2026.csv"
if (!file.exists(raw_file)) {
  zip_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
  download.file(url, zip_file, mode = "wb")
  unzip(zip_file, exdir = "../data/raw")
}


```

```{r}
# Read the data.
orders <- read_csv(raw_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Analysis

```{r}
# Split before exploration and preprocessing.
set.seed(522)
train_rows <- sample(seq_len(nrow(orders)), size = floor(0.8 * nrow(orders)))
orders_train <- orders |> slice(train_rows)
orders_test <- orders |> slice(-train_rows)
```

```{r}
# Keep original order-time predictors and the target.
columns <- c(
  "metro_city", "cuisine_category", "order_channel", "order_value_usd",
  "discount_applied_usd", "delivery_distance_km", "estimated_prep_time_min",
  "delivery_fee_usd", "restaurant_price_tier", "is_peak_hour",
  "weather_condition", "estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd"
)
orders_train <- orders_train |>
  select(all_of(columns))
orders_test <- orders_test |>
  select(all_of(columns))

colSums(is.na(orders_train))
```

```{r}
write_csv(orders_train, "../data/processed/orders_train.csv")
write_csv(orders_test, "../data/processed/orders_test.csv")
```

## Dummy regression baseline

```{r}
set.seed(522)
folds <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(orders_train)))
dummy_rmse <- numeric(5)

for (i in 1:5) {
  train_margin <- orders_train$estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd[folds != i]
  validation_margin <- orders_train$estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd[folds == i]

  prediction <- mean(train_margin)
  dummy_rmse[i] <- sqrt(mean((validation_margin - prediction)^2))
}

data.frame(
  Model = "Mean baseline",
  Mean_RMSE_USD = mean(dummy_rmse),
  SD_RMSE_USD = sd(dummy_rmse)
)
```

Table 4. Five-fold cross-validation performance of the dummy model.

## Linear regression

```{r}
linear_rmse <- numeric(5)

for (i in 1:5) {
  fold_train <- orders_train |> filter(folds != i)
  fold_validation <- orders_train |> filter(folds == i)

  linear_model <- lm(estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd ~ ., data = fold_train)
  predictions <- predict(linear_model, newdata = fold_validation)
  linear_rmse[i] <- sqrt(mean(
    (fold_validation$estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd - predictions)^2
  ))
}

data.frame(
  Model = c("Mean baseline", "Linear regression"),
  Mean_RMSE_USD = c(mean(dummy_rmse), mean(linear_rmse)),
  SD_RMSE_USD = c(sd(dummy_rmse), sd(linear_rmse))
)
```

Table 5. Model performance using the same five cross-validation folds.

## Ridge regression

```{r}
lambdas <- 10^seq(2, -5, by = -1)
ridge_rmse <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = 5, ncol = length(lambdas))

for (i in 1:5) {
  fold_train <- orders_train |> filter(folds != i)
  fold_validation <- orders_train |> filter(folds == i)

  # Use training categories to encode both datasets.
  encoding <- lm(estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd ~ ., data = fold_train)
  x_train <- model.matrix(encoding)[, -1]
  x_validation <- model.matrix(
    delete.response(terms(encoding)), data = fold_validation,
    contrasts.arg = encoding$contrasts, xlev = encoding$xlevels
  )[, -1]

  ridge_model <- glmnet(
    x_train, fold_train$estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd,
    alpha = 0, lambda = lambdas, standardize = TRUE
  )
  predictions <- predict(ridge_model, newx = x_validation, s = lambdas)
  ridge_rmse[i, ] <- sqrt(colMeans(
    (predictions - fold_validation$estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd)^2
  ))
}

ridge_results <- data.frame(
  Lambda = lambdas,
  Mean_RMSE_USD = colMeans(ridge_rmse),
  SD_RMSE_USD = apply(ridge_rmse, 2, sd)
)
ridge_results |> arrange(Mean_RMSE_USD)
```

Table 6. Ridge penalties compared using five-fold cross-validation.

## Model comparison

```{r}
best_ridge <- ridge_results |> slice_min(Mean_RMSE_USD, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
best_lambda <- best_ridge$Lambda

model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Mean baseline", "Linear regression", "Ridge regression"),
  Mean_RMSE_USD = c(mean(dummy_rmse), mean(linear_rmse), best_ridge$Mean_RMSE_USD),
  SD_RMSE_USD = c(sd(dummy_rmse), sd(linear_rmse), best_ridge$SD_RMSE_USD)
)
model_comparison |> arrange(Mean_RMSE_USD)
best_lambda
```

Table 7. Comparison of the three models on the same training-data folds.

## Final test evaluation

```{r}
final_model <- lm(estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd ~ ., data = orders_train)
test_predictions <- predict(final_model, newdata = orders_test)
dummy_predictions <- rep(mean(orders_train$estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd),
                         nrow(orders_test))
test_margin <- orders_test$estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd

test_scores <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Linear regression", "Mean baseline"),
  RMSE_USD = c(sqrt(mean((test_margin - test_predictions)^2)),
               sqrt(mean((test_margin - dummy_predictions)^2))),
  MAE_USD = c(mean(abs(test_margin - test_predictions)),
              mean(abs(test_margin - dummy_predictions))),
  R_squared = c(1 - sum((test_margin - test_predictions)^2) /
                  sum((test_margin - mean(test_margin))^2),
                1 - sum((test_margin - dummy_predictions)^2) /
                  sum((test_margin - mean(test_margin))^2))
)
test_scores
```

Table 8. Final performance on the held-out test orders.

```{r}
x_train <- model.matrix(final_model)[, -1]
x_test <- model.matrix(
  delete.response(terms(final_model)), data = orders_test,
  contrasts.arg = final_model$contrasts, xlev = final_model$xlevels
)[, -1]
final_ridge <- glmnet(
  x_train, orders_train$estimated_restaurant_net_margin_usd,
  alpha = 0, lambda = lambdas, standardize = TRUE
)
ridge_predictions <- as.numeric(predict(final_ridge, newx = x_test, s = best_lambda))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Test predictions from all three models. The dashed line represents perfect predictions. Linear and Ridge predictions nearly overlap; Ridge uses the penalty selected by training-data cross-validation."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
data.frame(
  actual_margin = test_margin,
  `Dummy baseline` = dummy_predictions,
  `Linear regression` = test_predictions,
  `Ridge regression` = ridge_predictions,
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  pivot_longer(-actual_margin, names_to = "Model", values_to = "Prediction") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = actual_margin, y = Prediction, colour = Model, shape = Model)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Dummy baseline" = "#009E73",
                                 "Linear regression" = "#0072B2",
                                 "Ridge regression" = "#D55E00")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Dummy baseline" = 16,
                                "Linear regression" = 1,
                                "Ridge regression" = 3)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(x = "Dataset-estimated net margin (USD)", y = "Predicted net margin (USD)")
```
